content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E032 (Keith Mclaughlin) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes with conflicting information:
- Note 1 (HR-ish): full-time Analyst, recommends write.
- Note 2 (Security DB): contractor with basic security training, recommends read.

The Security note says the employee is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training caps access at read.

Wait — but note 2 also says "role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)". Hmm, the roles are different: note 1 is from HR agent? Actually the notes are from HR agent and Security agent. Note 2 seems to be from Security agent, who looked up employment type in their own database and found contractor. Note 1 said full_time (looked up in own database). These conflict.

The security training is basic, so per policy: contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin. So max for contractor with basic training = read.

Requested write > max read, so grant maximum = read.

So the decision is read.

Let me submit read with a reason explaining that the security DB indicates contractor with basic training, so max is read, requested write exceeds, grant read.
